OTHER TIES: NAMED IN A CASE, PRINTS ITS MONEY, AUDITS OR MANAGES FUNDS (ROYAL MONETARY AUTHORITY OF BHUTAN (BHUTAN))
Source says: Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan (Bhutan). The Royal Government of Bhutan appoints or directs the board of the Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan (Bhutan). The Royal Monetary Authority Act of Bhutan 2010, passed by Parliament on 2 June 2010 and in force from 22 June 2010, lets the executive direct the central bank: section 149 says the Royal Government may from time to time issue such directives to the Authority as it may consider necessary after consultation with the Governor, in the public interest, and must report them to Parliament. Of the Board's seven members, four are appointed by the Government and one of those must come from the Ministry of Finance. The Governor is appointed by the Druk Gyalpo on the Prime Minister's recommendation, and may be removed the same way, though only on a finding by a committee of permanent incapacity, incapability of carrying out the duties, or breach of the code of conduct. The Royal Government sets the Governor's salary and the board members' fees. The Act repealed the 1982 Royal Monetary Authority Act. This is a standing arrangement with no end date. The Royal Monetary Authority Act of Bhutan 2010 (Parliament of Bhutan)
